# Benchmarks: ISLA against GeoTransolver and Transolver {#sec-scoreboard}

**With every architecture fed the same inputs and scored on the same
float32 instrument, GeoTransolver and plain Transolver are at least as
accurate as ISLA on every in-distribution surface benchmark this program has
measured, from 2% at the 512-wide, 80,000-cell corner against the
constant-gauge variant of ISLA (5% against the reference configuration,
which trains there at the width learning rate) to 28% at 35
HiLift cases (against ISLA's reference configuration, the relative frame);
ISLA is ahead where geometries arrive in arbitrary poses (6% and 19%,
constant-gauge variant), on interior velocity (27%, reference configuration
with query tokens), and on consistency under a change of surface sampling,
where its reference frame degrades 1.2x against 10 to 16x for every
configuration that centres its coordinates on the sampled points.** This
chapter is the scoreboard. It collects every cross-architecture measurement
of the book on one page, computed from the same result files the evidence
chapters use, so that a reader who needs the standing of ISLA against the
two mainstream mesh transformers can take it from here and go to
@sec-data-efficiency, @sec-full-data and @sec-interior only for the protocol
behind a particular row.

## How to read every number {#sec-scoreboard-protocol}

Four conventions hold for every table and figure below.

**The metric** is the relative L2 error of surface pressure defined in
@sec-metrics: cell-area-weighted over the sampled points of a case, so it
scores error per unit surface area, and averaged arithmetically over the
validation cases of the split (@sec-splits). Interior rows use the same
relative L2 on interior pressure, velocity and eddy viscosity over the
sampled interior points. Every value is a float32 inference on the
final-epoch checkpoint, the reporting instrument of @sec-metrics; no
bfloat16 number appears here.

**The inputs are matched.** Every model receives the freestream as a unit
direction, the protocol requirement of @sec-fair-comparison; no
physical-velocity baseline appears below. Tokens per case (10,000 sampled
cells unless a row says otherwise), epochs (500), split and validation
cases are identical across architectures in every row; each architecture
runs at its own best learning rate. At 1,260 HiLift cases both
GeoTransolver and ISLA's constant-gauge variant were also trained at
20,000 cells: each improves by about 5% and their ratio does not move
(0.885 against 0.878), so the rows below are not a cell-count floor
(@sec-nb-w2c-floor-verdict).

**A ratio is baseline error divided by ISLA error**, so a value above one
favours ISLA and a value below one favours the baseline. Where a rung was
also run on further random training draws, the ratio carries the 90%
interval over draws, which is three to eleven times wider than the seed
spread at 35 cases and is the uncertainty to read.

**Which ISLA.** ISLA's reference configuration is the relative frame with
the total-measure length scale (@sec-mt2-forward): no centroid, no sample
statistic anywhere in the frame, so its output does not depend on how the
surface was sampled. It is measured on eight of the nine surface rungs
below: 35 and 210 HiLift cases, 4 and 21 training geometries, the fixed
angle, DrivAerML at 435 cars under the independent and the stratified
inference draw, and the 512-wide, 80,000-cell corner (under the width
learning rate). Its price against the constant-gauge
variant (@sec-mt2-variants) splits by whether the validation geometries
recur in training: none on DrivAerML at the reference size, 3% at the
corner (4% at a matched learning rate, @sec-nb-cg-wlr-verdict), 1% at 4
geometries and 5% at 21 geometries (never-seen validation geometries), 11%
at both 35 and 210 cases, where the validation geometries recur, and 14.5%
at the fixed angle (three seeds), where a single freestream direction makes
the mesher's refinement pattern a reusable cue; on both splits tested with an exact full-geometry
frame the price is the plain mean's mesher pattern, not positional
information (@sec-nb-frame-full-verdict,
@sec-nb-frame-full-fixed-angle-verdict, @sec-nb-relframe-ladder-verdict).
Where a rung has both, the tables give the reference configuration and the
constant-gauge variant side by side; on the 510-case and 1,260-case rungs
only the constant-gauge variant, which centres on the plain mean of the
sampled points, is measured, and the tables say so; at the corner the
reference configuration is measured under the width learning rate
(@sec-nb-corner-wlr-verdict). Two further
configurations appear where they inform the reading: the baselines with
the surface measure carried in their slice pooling (research variants that
locate a property, @sec-part-baseline; the released GeoTransolver and
Transolver are not modified, @sec-nb-ruling-released-baselines), and ISLA
with its measure weights off, an ablation that reads the mesh density, is
never adopted (@sec-principle), and is shown only to price the measure
semantics.

def ratio(b, i): return mean(b) / mean(i)

The resources behind the comparison are in @tbl-scoreboard-resources: the
three architectures are parameter-matched at the reference width, and ISLA
trains in the least memory once its geometry blocks are recomputed in the
backward pass. The table measures the eager path on which all three
architectures can be run on one instrument; on the compiled path the recipe
runs, ISLA's training step is 1.05x GeoTransolver's at 10,000 tokens (47
against 45 ms at 1.30 against 2.70 GiB) and 0.86x without the geometry
recompute (@sec-mt2-cost).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scoreboard-resources
#| output: asis
def cfg(name, tokens):
    return next(c for c in cost["configs"] if c["name"] == name and c["tokens"] == tokens)
rows = [("ISLA, hidden 192 (fast point softmax)", "isla_h192_fast_plain"),
        ("ISLA, hidden 192, geometry blocks recomputed in backward", "isla_h192_fast_ckpt"),
        ("GeoTransolver, hidden 256", "gt_h256"),
        ("Transolver, hidden 256", "transolver_h256")]
out = "| configuration | parameters | step at 10,000 tokens [ms] | peak memory at 10,000 tokens [GiB] | step at 80,000 tokens [ms] | peak memory at 80,000 tokens [GiB] |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n"
for label, name in rows:
    a, b = cfg(name, 10000), cfg(name, 80000)
    out += (f"| {label} | {a['n_params']/1e6:.1f}M | {statistics.median(a['step_ms']):.0f} | {max(a['incremental_peak_allocated_bytes'])/2**30:.2f} "
            f"| {statistics.median(b['step_ms']):.0f} | {max(b['incremental_peak_allocated_bytes'])/2**30:.1f} |\n")
print(out)
print(": Training cost of the three architectures on one instrument and one execution path: one "
      "GB300 GPU, eager execution, batch of one case, bfloat16 autocast, AdamW step, median of five "
      "measured steps after three warm-up steps; memory is the peak allocated during the step net of "
      "the resident parameters and optimizer state. The three reference-width models are within 9.0M, "
      "8.9M and 6.0M parameters. The recomputed-geometry row is the same function at a lower memory "
      "and a higher step time. The path the recipe trains on is the compiled one, where ISLA's step is "
      "1.05x GeoTransolver's at 10,000 tokens with the recompute on and 0.86x without, at 1.30 and 1.94 "
      "GiB against GeoTransolver's 2.70 GiB (@sec-mt2-cost; results/kernel_study_2026-09-13/pareto_gb300_full_bf16.json). "
      "Data: results/isla_vs_baselines_cost_fastkernel_2026-09-09.json. {#tbl-scoreboard-resources}")
```

## Surface pressure: every rung on one axis {#sec-scoreboard-surface}

**On eight of eight surface settings the unit-direction baselines match or beat
ISLA; the margin runs from 28% at 35 HiLift cases against the reference
configuration (20% against the constant-gauge variant) and 25% at 4
training geometries (the same against the reference configuration and the
constant-gauge variant, which are at parity there) to 2% against the
constant-gauge variant and 5% against the reference configuration at the
512-wide, 80,000-cell corner, and it does not close as the training set
grows from 35 to 210 cases.**
@fig-scoreboard-forest places every setting on one axis of baseline error
divided by ISLA error, and @tbl-scoreboard-surface gives the numbers, seeds
and paired case counts behind each marker.

```{python}
#| label: fig-scoreboard-forest
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The scoreboard on one axis. Each row is one benchmark setting; each
#|   marker is a baseline's surface-pressure error divided by ISLA's on the
#|   same validation cases (GeoTransolver red circles, Transolver grey
#|   triangles), so markers left of the line at 1 favour the baseline and
#|   markers right of it favour ISLA. Filled markers divide by ISLA's
#|   reference configuration (relative frame, total-measure scale); open
#|   markers divide by the constant-gauge variant, which on the 510-case and
#|   corner rows is the only ISLA measured. Horizontal bars at 35 and 210 cases are the
#|   90% interval of the ratio over four random training draws (three seeds
#|   each), the honest uncertainty at those rungs; other rows carry the
#|   seed-mean ratio only. The bottom three rows are the interior task
#|   (GeoTransolver-volume divided by ISLA with query tokens and the signed
#|   distance) and the pose test (baselines trained with SO(3) augmentation,
#|   ISLA without, every case in a random pose). How to read this: it shows
#|   ratios, not absolute accuracy, and says nothing about consistency under
#|   a change of sampling (@fig-scoreboard-density). Float32 throughout.
#|   Data: the files listed in @tbl-scoreboard-surface, plus
#|   research/transfer_program/studies/campaign_a_draws/campaign_a_n{35,210}_fp32_2026-09-10.json,
#|   research/transfer_program/studies/campaign_b_pose/campaign_b_fp32_2026-09-10.json and
#|   results/fp32_reeval/fp32_shift_interior_2026-09-09.json.
#| code-fold: true

INK, INK2, MUTED, GRID, BASELINE = "#0b0b0b", "#52514e", "#898781", "#e1e0d9", "#c3c2b7"
mpl.rcParams.update({"figure.dpi": 110, "font.size": 10, "axes.edgecolor": BASELINE,
                     "axes.labelcolor": INK2, "axes.grid": True, "grid.color": GRID,
                     "xtick.color": MUTED, "ytick.color": MUTED, "xtick.labelcolor": INK2,
                     "ytick.labelcolor": INK2, "axes.spines.top": False,
                     "axes.spines.right": False, "legend.frameon": False})

    s = S[key]; i = s[against]
    ci = s["draws"]
    rows.append((label, ratio(s["gt"], i), (ratio(s["t"], i) if s["t"] else None), against == "isla_ref",
                 (ci[0]["ci90"] if ci and against == "isla_cg" else None),
                 (ci[1]["ci90"] if ci and against == "isla_cg" else None)))
add("HiLift, 35 cases — vs reference ISLA", "hl35", "isla_ref")

add("HiLift, 210 cases — vs reference ISLA", "hl210", "isla_ref")
add("HiLift, 210 cases — vs constant-gauge variant", "hl210", "isla_cg")

add("HiLift, 1,260 cases — vs constant-gauge variant", "hl1260", "isla_cg")
add("HiLift, 4 training geometries — vs reference ISLA", "geo4", "isla_ref")
add("HiLift, 4 training geometries — vs constant-gauge variant", "geo4", "isla_cg")
add("HiLift, 21 training geometries — vs reference ISLA", "geo21", "isla_ref")
add("HiLift, 21 training geometries — vs constant-gauge variant", "geo21", "isla_cg")
add("HiLift, fixed angle 12° — vs reference ISLA", "fixed", "isla_ref")
add("HiLift, fixed angle 12° — vs constant-gauge variant", "fixed", "isla_cg")
add("DrivAerML, 435 cars — vs reference ISLA", "dr435", "isla_ref")
add("DrivAerML, 435 cars — vs constant-gauge variant", "dr435", "isla_cg")
add("DrivAerML, 435 cars, stratified inference draw — vs reference ISLA", "dr435_strat", "isla_ref")
add("DrivAerML, 435 cars, stratified inference draw — vs constant-gauge variant", "dr435_strat", "isla_cg")
add("DrivAerML, 512 wide × 80k cells — vs reference ISLA (width learning rate)", "corner", "isla_ref")
add("DrivAerML, 512 wide × 80k cells — vs constant-gauge variant", "corner", "isla_cg")
# pose: baselines with augmentation in random poses ÷ ISLA without, in random poses
pB = poseB["arms"]
rows.append(("DrivAerML, every case in a random pose", pB["gt_aug"]["pressure_mean"] / pB["isla"]["pressure_mean"],
             pB["transolver_aug"]["pressure_mean"] / pB["isla"]["pressure_mean"], False, None, None))
# interior: GeoTransolver-volume (unit direction) ÷ ISLA query tokens + SDF, two seeds, fp32
def intf(keys, f): return mean(fp(fpint, keys, f))
gtv = [f"udrv_gt_vol_seed{s}" for s in (42, 43)]; isq = [f"v0_isla_qtsdfval_seed{s}" for s in (42, 43)]
# filled marker: ISLA's interior reference configuration (relative frame, total-measure scale; relint2 artifact);
# open marker: the similarity-gauge interior variant
for f, lab in (("pressure_l2", "interior pressure"), ("velocity_l2", "interior velocity"), ("nut_l2", "interior eddy viscosity")):
    rows.append((f"DrivAerML interior, {lab} — vs reference ISLA", ri2["gt_vol_unit"][f]["mean"] / ri2["relint2"][f]["mean"], None, True, None, None))
    rows.append((f"DrivAerML interior, {lab} — vs similarity-gauge variant", intf(gtv, f) / intf(isq, f), None, False, None, None))
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9.2, 6.4))

#| label: tbl-scoreboard-surface

def fmt(v):
    if not v: return "pending"
    return f"{mean(v):.4f}" + (" (" + " / ".join(f"{x:.4f}" for x in v) + ")" if len(v) > 1 else "")
def rat(b, s, ci):
    if not b: return "pending"
    parts = []
    if s["isla_ref"]: parts.append(f"**{ratio(b, s['isla_ref']):.2f}**")
    parts.append(f"{ratio(b, s['isla_cg']):.2f}" + (f" [{ci['ci90'][0]:.2f}–{ci['ci90'][1]:.2f}]" if ci else ""))
    return " ‖ ".join(parts)
out = ("| setting | GeoTransolver | Transolver | ISLA, reference configuration | ISLA, constant-gauge variant | GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA (reference ‖ constant gauge) | Transolver ÷ ISLA (reference ‖ constant gauge) | validation cases where the baseline is lower |\n"
       "|---|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|\n")
for key in ("hl35", "hl210", "hl510", "hl1260", "geo4", "geo21", "fixed", "dr435", "dr435_strat", "corner"):
    s = S[key]
    ref = f"**{fmt(s['isla_ref'])}**" if s["isla_ref"] else "not yet measured"
    cg, ct = s["draws"] if s["draws"] else (None, None)
    out += (f"| {s['title']} | {fmt(s['gt'])} | {fmt(s['t'])} | {ref} | {fmt(s['isla_cg'])} "
            f"| {rat(s['gt'], s, cg)} | {rat(s['t'], s, ct)} | {s['paired'][0]} |\n")
print(out)
print(": Surface-pressure relative L2 (float32, final-epoch checkpoints, seed values in "
      "parentheses; the corner row lists seed means of two seeds) on every rung where the "
      "unit-direction baselines and ISLA are both measured. The ratio columns give baseline ÷ ISLA "
      "against the reference configuration in bold on the eight rungs where it is measured (35 and "
      "210 HiLift cases, 4 and 21 training geometries, the fixed angle, 435 DrivAerML cars under the "
      "independent and the stratified inference draw, the 512 × 80k corner) and "
      "against the constant-gauge variant on every rung; brackets are the 90% interval of the "
      "constant-gauge ratio over four random training draws (35 and 210 cases; at 35 cases the "
      "draws used GeoTransolver's 1e-3 lane). GeoTransolver runs at 3e-3 on the 35-case rung and "
      "1e-3 elsewhere on HiLift, 1e-3 on DrivAerML; Transolver at 3e-3 everywhere; ISLA at 1e-3. "
      "The corner row is width 512 and 80,000 cells per car for all arms (ISLA with the fast "
      "point-softmax kernel; 60.2M, 35.9M and 23.9M parameters), evaluated at 80,000 cells; the "
      "reference configuration there trained at the width learning rate 3.75e-4 after diverging at "
      "the protocol rate 1e-3, the other arms at their protocol rates (@sec-nb-corner-wlr-verdict); the "
      "constant-gauge variant retrained at 3.75e-4 scores 0.0424, so the rate costs it nothing and the "
      "reference's excess is the frame's (@sec-nb-cg-wlr-verdict; control, not a row). "
      "The stratified-draw row queries the same 435-car checkpoints with a systematic sample along the "
      "Morton order of the cells (same inclusion law and weights as the independent draw): every model "
      "improves, the baselines by 2% and ISLA by 4% (@sec-nb-quadvar-verdict); the headline ratios of this "
      "book are the independent-draw rows. The 27–218-car DrivAerML ladder has no unit-direction "
      "baseline measurement and is not listed. Data: "
      + "; ".join(sorted({S[k]['src'] for k in S})) + ". {#tbl-scoreboard-surface}")
```

What the DrivAerML gap at the reference size is made of. Of the 9 to 10
points by which GeoTransolver leads ISLA's constant-gauge variant at
10,000 independently drawn cells, about two are the metric's own
finite-sample estimator (every architecture improves by 2% under a
lower-variance draw of the same cells), about two are ISLA's slice-integral
variance at that budget (the stratified-draw row above removes them), about
three are the residual count dependence that only more cells remove (the
ratio is 0.955 at 40,000 cells), and four to five are the trained
function's, which the capacity ladder attributes to width, an axis that
moves every architecture alike, and not to the slice count, depth or MLP
width (@sec-nb-deficit-anatomy, @sec-nb-cap-verdict, @sec-nb-quadvar-verdict);
of those four to five, about two and a half are the positional information
the invariance contracts deny the model (a raw-coordinate diagnostic
recovers them, at a 13x density collapse, @sec-nb-eqprice-verdict) and
about two are the slice-attention form.
The frame contributes nothing on DrivAerML at this size. At deployment
resolution the deficit is therefore 4 to 5%, and at the scale corner 2 to
5%; the 25 to 28% at 35 HiLift cases is a different mechanism, the
mesher-pattern cue where geometries recur (@sec-nb-frame-full-verdict).

Two facts qualify the table. First, the measure-weighted baselines, which
carry the same quadrature measure in their slice pooling that ISLA does,
keep the lead: at 35 HiLift cases they score
`{python} f"{mean(S['hl35']['gt_mw']):.3f}"` and
`{python} f"{mean(S['hl35']['t_mw']):.3f}"` (three seeds each; a 6.5% price
for the measure) against the reference ISLA's
`{python} f"{mean(S['hl35']['isla_ref']):.3f}"`, and on DrivAerML
`{python} f"{mean(S['dr435']['gt_mw']):.4f}"` and
`{python} f"{mean(S['dr435']['t_mw']):.4f}"` at no price against
`{python} f"{mean(S['dr435']['isla_ref']):.4f}"`. Second, the ISLA
weights-off ablation is not in the table because it is not a configuration
the program adopts: it closes a third to all of the gap on the HiLift rungs
(0.1224 at 35 cases, 0.0589 at 210, 0.0905 at 21 geometries, 0.0311 at the
fixed angle, 0.2078 at 4 geometries) by reading the mesher's cell pattern,
and under a change of sampling it collapses hardest of every configuration
measured (@sec-scoreboard-consistency, @sec-limits-mechanism).

## Interior fields from the surface {#sec-scoreboard-interior}

**On the boundary-to-interior task ISLA's reference configuration, with
its interior queries admitted as interacting tokens and given the signed
distance to the wall, is 27% more accurate than GeoTransolver's volume
configuration on interior velocity at a third of the parameters (0.0782
against 0.1070), 7% less accurate on interior pressure (0.0550 against
0.0513) and 14% less accurate on eddy viscosity (0.1005 against 0.0879;
GeoTransolver-volume ÷ ISLA 0.93, 1.37 and 0.87; two seeds, float32;
@sec-nb-relint-verdict). The similarity-gauge interior variant matches it
on pressure and velocity and trails it by 12% on eddy viscosity; at
parameters matched to GeoTransolver-volume that variant leads on pressure
and velocity and trails on eddy viscosity by 18%, the whole of which sits
in the far wake.** The task, the two architectures' interior modes and the
diagnostics are in @sec-interior; the numbers are in
@fig-scoreboard-interior and @tbl-scoreboard-interior. The interacting
decode's prediction at a point depends on the joint query set, so every
interior value holds at the training count of 10,000 queries, which is the
deployment count (@sec-nb-qcount-verdict).

## Arbitrary poses: where the contract earns accuracy {#sec-scoreboard-pose}

**When every training and validation case arrives in its own random
orientation, ISLA's error is unchanged and the augmented baselines' rises
by 20% and 31%, which makes ISLA 6% and 19% more accurate than
GeoTransolver and Transolver on the same posed cars.** This is ISLA's one
measured in-distribution accuracy lead over input-matched baselines, and it
is conditional on the setting: in a canonical frame the same baselines lead
(@sec-scoreboard-surface), and GeoTransolver trained in a canonicalized
frame is pose-invariant at a 1% cost (@sec-pose). ISLA's rotation and
translation covariance is exact by construction (@sec-mt2-contracts) and
needs no augmentation.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scoreboard-pose
#| output: asis
C = poseB["canonical"]; A = poseB["arms"]
def seeds(d): return " / ".join(f"{v['pressure_l2']:.4f}" for v in d["runs"].values())
rows = [("GeoTransolver, trained with SO(3) augmentation", C["gt"], A["gt_aug"]),
        ("Transolver, trained with SO(3) augmentation", C["transolver_lr3e3"], A["transolver_aug"]),
        ("ISLA, no augmentation (constant-gauge variant)", C["isla"], A["isla"])]
out = "| architecture | canonical pose | every case in a random SO(3) pose | posed ÷ canonical | baseline ÷ ISLA, posed |\n|---|---|---|---:|---:|\n"
for label, c, a in rows:
    out += (f"| {label} | {c['pressure_mean']:.4f} | {a['pressure_mean']:.4f} ({seeds(a)}) | {a['pressure_mean']/c['pressure_mean']:.2f} "
            f"| {a['pressure_mean']/A['isla']['pressure_mean']:.2f} |\n")
print(out)
print(": DrivAerML surface pressure, 435 training cars, 48 validation cars, float32. The canonical "
      "column is each architecture's unit-direction reference in the dataset's native frame (three seeds "
      "for GeoTransolver and ISLA, two for Transolver); the posed column trains and validates with "
      "every case rotated by its own random SO(3) element (two seeds each). GeoTransolver without "
      "augmentation scores 0.0631 in random poses and ISLA with augmentation 0.0578 (one seed each; "
      "in the artifact). Data: "
      "research/transfer_program/studies/campaign_b_pose/campaign_b_fp32_2026-09-10.json. "
      "{#tbl-scoreboard-pose}")
```

## Consistency under a change of surface sampling {#sec-scoreboard-consistency}

**Every configuration that centres its coordinates on a statistic of the
sampled points, whichever architecture it belongs to, degrades 10 to 19x
when the same surface is resampled with a 10:1 front-to-back density bias;
frames that read nothing from the sample hold at 1.1 to 1.2x, and the
baselines join that group once their datapipe centres on an unbiased
estimate of the geometric centroid.** Consistency in the fine-mesh limit
is the acceptance criterion of @sec-principle, not a score: a model whose
prediction depends on where the mesher happened to refine is not
predicting the physics. The probe holds the geometry fixed and redraws
10,000 cells with the bias, with exact Horvitz–Thompson weights so a
measure-consistent model sees the same surface integral; the ratio of the
error under the biased draw to the error under the uniform draw is the
number in @fig-scoreboard-density. Every ratio is stated in the sample
frame, the frame a biased mesher would deliver, in which the input is
centred on the drawn points.

```{python}

#|   error under the uniform draw, on a log axis; 1 is exact consistency and
#|   the grey band marks up to 1.5x. Bars are sample-frame values, the
#|   like-for-like convention in which every model's input is centred on the
#|   drawn points. Open markers on the baseline rows are the same
#|   checkpoints with the frame handed to them unbiased by the pipeline
#|   (pool frame), and the two rows marked "HT-centred datapipe" are
#|   baselines retrained with the datapipe centring on the Horvitz–Thompson
#|   estimate of the geometric centroid. Colour: ISLA blue, GeoTransolver
#|   red, Transolver grey; the weights-off ablation is hatched. How to read

    ("Transolver, unit direction", R["transolver_unit"]["density_factor"], R["transolver_unit"]["density_factor_pipeline_frame"], GREY, ""),
    ("GeoTransolver, measure-weighted pooling", R["geotransolver_unit_mw"]["density_factor"], R["geotransolver_unit_mw"]["density_factor_pipeline_frame"], RED, ""),

ax.axvspan(1.0, 1.5, color=GRID, alpha=0.7, zorder=0)
for yy, (label, sf, pf, c, h) in zip(y, items):
    ax.barh(yy, sf, height=0.62, color=c, alpha=0.85, hatch=h, edgecolor="white", zorder=2)
    ax.text(sf * 1.06, yy, f"{sf:.2f}x", va="center", fontsize=8.5, color=INK2)
    if pf:
        ax.plot([pf], [yy], marker="o", ms=7, mfc="white", mec=c, mew=1.8, ls="none", zorder=4)
        ax.text(pf, yy + 0.36, f"pool frame {pf:.1f}x", ha="center", fontsize=7.5, color=c)
ax.set_yticks(y); ax.set_yticklabels([i[0] for i in items], fontsize=8.5)
ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_xlim(0.9, 45)
ax.set_xticks([1, 1.5, 2, 5, 10, 20]); ax.set_xticklabels(["1", "1.5", "2", "5", "10", "20"])
ax.xaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter())
ax.axvline(1.0, color=INK2, lw=1.0, zorder=1)
ax.set_xlabel("error under 10:1 biased sampling ÷ error under uniform sampling (sample frame) [–]", color=INK2, fontsize=9.5)
ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

The single-count probe understates the question the principle asks, which
is whether the prediction converges to one field as the sample is refined
and to the same field under two sampling laws. The consistency benchmark
of @sec-consistency-bench evaluates every checkpoint at 2,500 to 40,000
cells under three samplers; @tbl-scoreboard-bench reads it at 40,000
cells, where a consistent configuration is within 3% of its own
uniform-sampling answer.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scoreboard-bench
#| output: asis
def bench(path): return J("consistency_bench/" + path)["arms"]
B0, Bmw, Bmc, Brf = (bench("consistency_bench_2026-09-10.json"), bench("consistency_bench_mw_2026-09-10.json"),
                     bench("consistency_bench_mcenter_2026-09-10.json"), bench("consistency_bench_rf_2026-09-11.json"))
def D(arms, arm, sampler, count="40000"):
    t = arms[arm]["table"]; return t[sampler][count]["pressure_l2"]["mean"] / t["unif"][count]["pressure_l2"]["mean"] - 1
def cell(arms, arm):
    return f"{D(arms, arm, 'area'):+.0%} / {D(arms, arm, 'biased'):+.0%}"
rows = [
    ("ISLA, reference configuration (relative frame, total-measure scale)", "in-model, none", (Brf, "rf_dr_mt2_meas"), (Brf, "rf_hl_mt2_meas_super_scarce")),
    ("ISLA, constant gauge, measure-weighted centring", "in-model, HT centroid", (Bmc, "cg_dr_mt2_mcenter"), (Bmc, "cg_hl_mt2_mcenter_super_scarce")),
    ("ISLA, similarity gauge (lr 3e-3)", "in-model, HT centroid and scale", (B0, "iw_mt2_gauge"), None),
    ("ISLA, constant-gauge variant", "in-model, plain mean", (B0, "iw_mt2_lr1e3"), (B0, "lad_hl_mt2_super_scarce")),
    ("ISLA, measure weights off (ablation)", "in-model, plain mean", (B0, "now_mt2_lr1e3"), (B0, "a35_hl_mt2_noweights")),
    ("GeoTransolver, unit direction", "pipeline pool mean (unbiased)", (B0, "uw_gt_unit_lr1e3"), (B0, "udrv_hl_gt_super_scarce_lr3e3")),
    ("Transolver, unit direction", "pipeline pool mean (unbiased)", (B0, "uw_transolver_unit_lr3e3"), (B0, "udrv_hl_transolver_super_scarce_lr3e3")),
    ("GeoTransolver, measure-weighted pooling", "pipeline pool mean (unbiased)", (Bmw, "mw_dr_gt_unit_lr1e3"), (Bmw, "mw_hl_gt_super_scarce_lr3e3")),
    ("Transolver, measure-weighted pooling", "pipeline pool mean (unbiased)", (Bmw, "mw_dr_transolver_unit_lr3e3"), (Bmw, "mw_hl_transolver_super_scarce_lr3e3")),
]
out = "| configuration | frame convention in the benchmark | DrivAerML: area / biased | HiLift 35 cases: area / biased |\n|---|---|---:|---:|\n"
for label, frame, dr, hl in rows:
    out += f"| {label} | {frame} | {cell(*dr)} | {cell(*hl) if hl else 'not run'} |\n"
print(out)
print(": Sampling-distribution dependence at 40,000 cells, float32, two seeds: the change in "
      "surface-pressure error when the same surface is drawn proportionally to cell area (area) or "
      "with the 10:1 front/back bias (biased) instead of uniformly over cells, as a percentage of the "
      "uniform-draw error; within ±3% counts as consistent. The frame column states where each "
      "model's input frame came from in this benchmark: the baselines received their centre from the "
      "pipeline's uniform 320,000-cell pool before the draw, an unbiased frame that a biased mesher "
      "would not deliver (their sample-frame sensitivity is the bar in @fig-scoreboard-density), while "
      "ISLA computes its frame in the model from the drawn points. With the frame held, measure "
      "weighting makes the baselines' aggregation consistent; the frame is the separate defect. Data: "
      "results/consistency_bench/consistency_bench_2026-09-10.json and its _mw, _mcenter and _rf "
      "companions. {#tbl-scoreboard-bench}")
```

Read together, the two instruments say one thing: the sampling-law
dependence of every architecture at the reference size lives in the input
frame, not in the attention. Measure weighting in the slice pooling repairs
the aggregation for the Transolver family at no accuracy cost on DrivAerML
and 6.5% on the wings; a frame that is a property of the geometry rather
than of the sample, whether ISLA's relative frame or a Horvitz–Thompson
centroid in the baselines' datapipe, removes the rest. The
Horvitz–Thompson-centred baselines are research variants that locate the
property; the released GeoTransolver and Transolver keep their plain-mean
frame and are not modified (@sec-nb-ruling-released-baselines), so the
deployable comparison is the released baselines against ISLA's reference
frame. On
the wings the reference frame's convergence is measured on the fixed-angle
split: from 2,500 to 40,000 cells its area-sampler deviation falls from
+45% to +2.6% and its biased-sampler deviation from +81% to +5.5%,
converging but not yet at the bias bar at 40,000, while it is the most
accurate arm under every sampler at every count
(@sec-nb-relframe-ladder-fixed-angle-bench;
`results/consistency_bench/consistency_bench_rffa_2026-09-11.json`).

## What is not yet on the board {#sec-scoreboard-pending}

Three measurements are not yet made, and one line is closed
(@sec-program-status). The 1,260-case HiLift rung has no unit-direction
baseline measurement, so it carries no comparison in this chapter. ISLA's
reference configuration is not yet measured on 510 or 1,260 HiLift cases or
at the 512-wide, 80,000-cell corner; on those rungs the ISLA value is the
constant-gauge variant's, and at the corner that variant is within 3% of
both baselines. At the corner the reference configuration diverged at the
protocol learning rate on both seeds, a width-driven hardening of the slice
routing that a lower rate removes (@sec-nb-relframe-divergence-matrix,
@sec-nb-relframe-divergence-mechanism); it is training under the width
learning-rate rule $10^{-3} \times 192/512$ with a preregistered parity bar
(@sec-nb-corner-wlr-prereg). The 1,260-case unit-direction GeoTransolver
pair has one seed trained and scored (float32 pressure 0.0348 against the
ISLA priors' 0.0393 and 0.0417) and the second within a day; the Transolver
pair follows (@sec-program-status). The baselines' consistency with a Horvitz–Thompson centroid
is measured on DrivAerML only, and only as a research variant: the released
GeoTransolver and Transolver keep their plain-mean frame and are not
modified (@sec-nb-ruling-released-baselines), so the "HT-centred datapipe"
rows locate a property, they do not describe a deployable model. The closed
line is the far-wake deficit that carries ISLA's interior eddy-viscosity
gap: the one remedy tested, oversampling the far field in the interior
training queries with exact measure weights, makes every field worse
(@sec-nb-farwake-verdict). Trained that way and scored on the standard
uniform interior sample, ISLA is worse than the similarity-gauge interior
variant it was built from on every field and in every wall-distance band
(recipe pressure, velocity and eddy viscosity
`{python} f"{fw['two_seed_mean']['pressure_l2']/fw['reference_three_seed_fp32']['pressure_l2']-1:+.0%}"`,
`{python} f"{fw['two_seed_mean']['velocity_l2']/fw['reference_three_seed_fp32']['velocity_l2']-1:+.0%}"` and
`{python} f"{fw['two_seed_mean']['nut_l2']/fw['reference_three_seed_fp32']['nut_l2']-1:+.0%}"`;
far-shell eddy viscosity beyond 0.4 body lengths
`{python} f"{fs['isla_farwake']['mean']['nut']['>=0.4L']['rel_l2']:.3f}"` against
`{python} f"{fs['isla_ref']['mean']['nut']['>=0.4L']['rel_l2']:.3f}"` for the
similarity-gauge variant and
`{python} f"{fs['gt_unit']['mean']['nut']['>=0.4L']['rel_l2']:.3f}"` for
GeoTransolver-volume; float32, two seeds,
`results/farwake_reduction_2026-09-11.json` and
`results/farwake_far_field_shells_2026-09-11.json`). The arm trains the
interacting decode on one query law and scores it on another, so it
settles the deployable question and not the mechanism, and it has no
baseline twin, which is why it is a closed line here and not a row above.
No row above depends on the weights-off ablation, on a bfloat16
evaluation, or on a physical-velocity baseline.
